title: Derived base-change pasting before unit cancellation
statement: Choose the derived categories of modules [def-pc-derived-category] on schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $f:X\to S$, $g:S'\to S$, $p:P\to X$, $q:P\to S'$ satisfy $h:pf=qg$, and let $t:T\to P$ be any morphism. Write $L_s=Ls^*$ and $R_s=Rs_*$ [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Take the pinned adjunctions $a_s:L_s\dashv R_s$ used in [def-pc-derived-base-change-map], with unit $\eta_s$, and the selected coherent comparisons $c(r,s):L_r\circ L_s\cong L_{rs}$ [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition]. Let $k:R_{tq}\cong R_q\circ R_t$ be the right-adjoint conjugate of $c(t,q)$, using $a_{tq}$ and the composite adjunction $L_t\circ L_q\dashv R_q\circ R_t$. For every $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, the canonical base-change mates satisfy $\beta(h_t)_E\,k_{L_{tp}E}\,R_q(R_t(c(t,p)^{-1}_E))=\beta(h)_E\,R_q(\eta_{t,L_pE})$, where $h_t:(tp)f=(tq)g$ is obtained by associativity from $h$. No cartesian or invertibility assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 08HY, counit description; Tag 0D5S, derived pullback composition

proof.text: Unfold the canonical counit transposes. The unit_conjugateEquiv identity and naturality show that conjugating a right adjoint carries its Hom equivalence to the composite Hom equivalence. Expand Adjunction.comp_homEquiv and use naturality on both factors to reduce the desired identity to c(t,q) followed by the composite-square transpose and c(t,p) inverse, equal to L_t of the original-square transpose.

Apply the two associativity laws of the selected c to (t,q,g) and (t,p,f). Equality-transport naturality of the family c(t,s) with respect to h identifies the middle comparison. Cancel the mapped isomorphism c(p,f) followed by c(t,pf); functoriality, inverse cancellation and transitivity of eqToHom prove the resulting comparison identity.

Naturality of c(t,p) inverse moves the counit of a_f through it. Postcompose the comparison identity by L_t L_p of this counit and apply both adjunction Hom equivalences. This proves the original pasting identity. Identity morphisms, empty schemes and zero E are covered by the same categorical identities.

theorem schemeDerivedBaseChange_pasting
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    {X S P S' T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S)
    (p : P ⟶ X) (q : P ⟶ S') (h : p ≫ f = q ≫ g) (t : T ⟶ P) :
    let c := @Classical.choose _ _ (Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec
      (Classical.choose_spec exists_derivedPullbackComposition)))
    let a := fun {A B : Scheme.{u}} (s : A ⟶ B) ↦
      Classical.choose (exists_schemeDerivedAdjunction s
        (hAdd := (Classical.choose exists_derivedPullbackComposition) s)
        ((Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec exists_derivedPullbackComposition)) s)
        ((Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec
          (Classical.choose_spec exists_derivedPullbackComposition))) s))
    let k := conjugateIsoEquiv (a (t ≫ q)) ((a q).comp (a t)) (c t q)
    ∀ E : schemeDerivedCategory X,
      schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f (t ≫ q) g (t ≫ p)
          (by rw [Category.assoc, h, Category.assoc]) E ≫
        k.hom.app ((derivedPullback (t ≫ p)).obj E) ≫
        (schemeDerivedDirectImage q).map
          ((schemeDerivedDirectImage t).map ((c t p).inv.app E)) =
      schemeDerivedBaseChangeMap f q g p h E ≫
        (schemeDerivedDirectImage q).map ((a t).unit.app ((derivedPullback p).obj E))
